KR.read: Korea's whole BPC market is anchored on a HIGH-confidence Euromonitor RETAIL figure of $13.0bn (2024), alongside a separately HIGH-confidence export figure of $11.43bn EXPORT_FOB (2025, MFDS/Korea Customs) - these sit on different value bases (domestic sell-through vs FOB shipments abroad) and are not additive. Per-capita spend of ~$250 (2024) is labelled an ESTIMATE derived in the baseline report, not a directly sourced figure. Two lower-confidence retail readings from Mordor Intelligence ($13.66bn, 2025) and Expert Market Research ($18.39bn, 2025) use a broader 'cosmetics' definition and are flagged value_basis_uncertain, so they sit alongside rather than override the Euromonitor anchor.
KR.trend: Observed domestic retail growth was a modest 1.8% YoY in constant-value terms (2024, HIGH confidence, Euromonitor), while export growth ran far hotter at +12.3% YoY (2025) and +20.3% YoY (2024), both HIGH confidence. A LOW-confidence Mordor Intelligence figure forecasts 6.61% CAGR for 2025-2030 - a forecast, not an observed rate, and tied to a broader product basket than the headline retail size.
KR.caveats: The HIGH-confidence retail total and the HIGH-confidence export total both look solid individually but measure different things and must not be combined or netted; the only forward-looking growth figure (CAGR) carries LOW confidence and a wider product definition than the headline market size.

IN.read: India's whole BPC market is sized at $33.08bn (2025) on a MEDIUM-confidence Statista/China Briefing RETAIL basis that the underlying data itself flags as value_basis_uncertain; no export figure exists at the India headline level. Per-capita spend of $22.74 (2025, MEDIUM confidence) is roughly an order of magnitude below Korea's, consistent with a much larger population base spreading the same order-of-magnitude-larger market size.
IN.trend: Observed growth is quoted at 10.0% YoY (2024) from a LOW-confidence baseline consensus that itself notes a spread across research houses (most cluster 10-11%, some conservative ones 5-6%). The cagr_forecast of 3.48% (2025-2030, MEDIUM confidence, Statista) is a forecast only, and is notably more conservative than both the observed 10% figure and the ~10% consensus the source itself references - implying an expected deceleration versus recent history.
IN.caveats: The headline market-size figure is MEDIUM confidence and explicitly flagged value-basis-uncertain (a Statista 'consumer market revenue' read, not a confirmed RETAIL sell-through number), and there is no export or independent per-capita cross-check at the headline level.

combined.read: Both headline market-size figures carry a value_usd_bn on a RETAIL basis, so a direct size comparison is possible: India's whole BPC market ($33.08bn, MEDIUM confidence, 2025) is roughly two and a half times the size of Korea's ($13.0bn, HIGH confidence, 2024), though the reference years differ by one and the confidence levels differ. Korea additionally carries a HIGH-confidence $11.43bn EXPORT_FOB total with no India counterpart in the headline data, so exports cannot enter this comparison. Both geographies show the same reconciliation tension: neither's top-down retail figure can be checked against its bottom-up sum, because the bottom-up bases differ in currency/unit and use NET_REALISATION rather than RETAIL, and in both cases that bottom-up sum is inflated by non-pure-play conglomerates reporting revenue well beyond BPC (LG H&H in Korea; Hindustan Unilever and Godrej Consumer Products in India) - both reconciliations are marked not publishable, with gap_pct left uncomputed rather than estimated. The Korea-India corridor does not appear in either headline block, but the raw data shows Korea's exports to India are a small, fast-growing slice (~$50m in H1 2025, +44.7% YoY) and several LOW/MEDIUM-confidence India-side estimates size the K-beauty-in-India [CORRIDOR] subset at roughly $0.3-0.4bn with high forecast CAGRs (19-26%, sources vary) - a fast-growing niche within, not representative of, either whole market.
